title: Fix the check that lets a bad one through

job.text: You asked the AI to check that the appointment date is in the future. The check it wrote is "the answer contains a date." A planted bad answer has a date — in the past (last year). Add a clause until the check fails that bad answer.

preview.text: The planted bad answer to catch: "Your appointment is set for March 14, 2025." — a real, nicely-formatted date, but in the past.
preview.more: the check already looks for: contains a date

naivePrompt: Check that it contains a date.
basePrompt: Check that it contains a date.

text.plain: AND the date is after today.
AND the date looks nicely formatted.
text.tech: AND it matches a date format

rules.claim: On last year's date: FAIL. On next week's date: PASS — but with extra clauses in the check.
rules.feedback: You found the clause that does the work, but you also kept 'formatted' or 'polite'. Neither looks at when — 'after today' is the one that separates a past date from a future one. Take them out so you know exactly which clause made the bad date fail.
rules.lesson: 'After today' does the work; 'formatted' and 'polite' just ride along — drop them.

cells: contains a date AND after today (+ extra clauses)

output.source: the right clause plus clauses that don't look at when

rules.claim: On last year's date: FAIL. On next week's date: PASS.
rules.feedback: Now it catches it. Adding "after today" is what tells a good date from a bad one. It fails last year's date and passes next week's.
rules.lesson: Tighten a check until the bad case fails it.

cells: contains a date AND after today

output.source: a check that looks at when

rules.feedback: Your check still lets the bad one through. The bad answer has a date — a nicely-formatted, politely-worded one, in the past. "Has a date" can't be enough; a formatted or polite clause doesn't look at when.
rules.lesson: If the bad answer satisfies the check, the check isn't tight enough.

output.source: a check that never looks at when

hints.nudge: The bad answer has a date too — so "has a date" can't be enough. What else is true of a good answer here?
hints.gap: Look again: the bad date is in the past. The check never looks at when.
hints.moves: Add …and the date is after today. Skip "formatted" and "polite" — they don't separate a past date from a future one.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "check it contains a date" → a past date sails through.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "…and the date is after today" → the past date fails.

template.plain: Your check passed this bad answer: [paste it]. That means the check is too loose. Tighten it so it FAILS this one, and show me it now failing.
template.tech: This bad input passed your check: [paste it]. Add the condition it ignores so the check returns False on it, then re-run and show it failing.

notes: ChatGPT: paste the bad answer and demand the check go red on it before you trust it.
Copilot in Excel: add the missing condition (e.g. >TODAY()) to the check formula and confirm the bad row flips to FALSE.
A chat AI that can't run code: ask "what is true of the bad answer that your check ignores?" — that gap is the clause to add. Never accept "I checked, it's fine."
